summary: Re-consideration of order dated 11.6.2022 in Petition No. 9/TT/2021 pursuant to the directions of Appellate Tribunal for Electricity in order dated 6.2.2023 in Appeal No. 362 of 2022. _The order under the appeal is set aside to the limited extent the appellant has been mulcted with a liability of Rs. 3.34 crores towards transmission charges, and the matter is remanded back to the Commission for its consideration afresh, and in accordance with law, on condition that the appellant pays PGCIL Rs.1.67 crores within three weeks from today. Needless to state that such payment, by the Appellant to PGCIL, shall be subject to the result of the petition before the Commission. We also make it clear that we have not expressed any opinion on the rival submissions and it is open to parties, on either side, to raise all such contentions as are available to them in law before the Commission.”_ 7. Pursuant to remand, Petition No. 9/TT/2021 was heard by the Commission on 22.5.2023 and 26.7.2023. The Commission vide the Record of Proceedings (RoP) dated 22.5.2023 directed AREPRL and PGCIL to file their respective written submissions. Sp. App. Writ No. 51/2020) and subsequent directives for land survey and allotment adjustments. Further, a series of Writ Petitions (S.B. Civil Writ Nos. 16304/2018 and 16305/2018) from villagers challenging the land allotments began in 2018. The High Court maintained a status quo order on the land, which prevented development work until the batch of writ petitions was disposed of vide common order dated 27.11.2019, thereby dismissing the batch of writ petitions. Following a further challenge in D.B. Sp. App. Writ Nos. 51/2020 and 52/2020, the High Court imposed another status quo vide order dated 25.2.2020, which remained operative until 29.6.2021. Thereafter, the Hon’ble Court directed the State Government to review land allotments affecting ESUCRL. 13. In response to the reply filed by ESUCRL, the Petitioner, in its rejoinder vide affidavit dated 19.7.2024, submitted as under: 14. The Petitioner in its Written Submissions dated 5.8.2024 has submitted as under: d) ESUCRL's Force Majeure claims, as raised in its reply dated 5.7.2024, do not impact Petitioner's statutory right to recover transmission charges for the mismatch period. This right stems from the Regulatory Approval Order dated 31.3.2016 (Petition No. 1/MP/2016) and relevant regulations. ESUCRL's claims of Force Majeure, including Right-of-Way (ROW) and court case delays, have already been considered in earlier tariff orders. APTEL judgment in _Fatehgarh Bhadla Transmission Co. Ltd. vs. Central Electricity Regulatory Commission_ has already clarified that transmission charges are recoverable for periods of mismatch when one entity's delay leaves the other’s assets stranded. These claims by ESUCRL, being separate from the current proceedings, should be raised in a separate petition, and cannot negate Petitioner’s right to recover transmission charges as approved by the Commission. 16. The Petitioner reiterated its submissions in the additional written statement dated 17. The final hearing in the matter was held on 8.8.2024, and subsequently, the order 18. Having heard the representatives for the Petitioner and Respondents, and having perused the material on record, we proceed to dispose of the Remand Petition. Considering the submissions of Petitioner and Respondents, the issues which arise for our consideration are as follows: 19. We have considered the submissions of the Petitioner, AREPRL and ESUCRL. The issues which arise for our consideration are as follows: ## 24. The relevant extracts of the regulatory approval order dated 31.3.2016 in Petition 39. The relevant extracts of the regulatory approval order dated 31.3.2016 in Petition generator are independent of the present proceedings claim and ought to be raised by ESUCRL in a separate Petition. The reliefs for the Force Majeure event (if any) can only be sought qua its beneficiaries, and the same cannot be claimed against the petitioner. Therefore, the aforesaid delays cannot in any way prejudice the rights of Petitioner to receive the transmission charges for the mismatch period, wherein Petitioner was ready with its assets, and the said assets could not be put into regular service due to the delay caused by ESUCRL. ESUCRL cannot wriggle out of its obligations to pay the transmission charges for the mismatch period in terms of the Regulations. 74. In view of the above discussions and findings, Petition No. 9/TT/2021, on remand, is disposed of. However, other terms and conditions of our earlier order dated 11.6.2022 shall remain unchanged.
